_doc: The ONE read-only policy shared by the Go agent and the Python control plane (#682, #691).
agent/go embeds this file; src/homepilot/adapters/readonly_policy.json must be a byte-identical copy
(tests/test_readonly_policy.py and agent/go/readonly_policy_test.go both fail on any drift).
Commands are POSITIVE-ONLY: a command is allowed only if its whole text matches its pattern.
Patterns use the syntax shared by Go RE2 and Python re, carry no anchors, and are matched against
the WHOLE command (Go wraps them in ^(?:...)$, Python uses fullmatch).
read_tier=false keeps a command out of the MCP read tier (exec_on_guest_readonly) while the agent
still accepts it from an admin caller. path_checked=true routes the argument through read_paths,
exactly like read_file. hint (optional) is the safe form a refusal of that command names, on both
layers, so a caller told no is also told what to ask for instead (#817).
read_paths is DEFAULT-DENY: a path must be in allow_exact or under allow_prefixes (or a write prefix),
and must not hit any deny rule. Deny rules always win, including over an operator's
HP_AGENT_READ_PREFIXES / HP_AGENT_WRITE_PREFIXES.
#818 widened read_paths to the build-defining config that holds no secrets by convention: the web
server (/etc/nginx), certbot renewal configs (/etc/letsencrypt/renewal: domains, authenticator, paths;
keys live in live/ and archive/, which stay unlisted), ufw (/etc/ufw), and update-notifier's pending
updates. The basename deny now also refuses any *secret*/*token*/*passw*/*credential* file and every
*.env / .env.* file, wherever it sits.

ps._doc: Read tier: process NAMES only, never command lines or environments (#817). argv carries other services' secrets (tokens passed as --flags), so every form names its columns with ONE -o from a fixed set that holds comm and never args/cmd/command/e; there is no BSD form (aux, ww, e) and no -f/-F. The full forms run only on a privileged agent, for an admin (agent/go/allowlist.go).
ps.hint: the read tier shows process names, never command lines (they carry other services' secrets): use ps -eo pid,user,comm,etime,pcpu,pmem (narrow with -p PID, -u USER or -C NAME; order with --sort=-pcpu)

ip._doc: Read verbs only (show/list/get). No set/add/del/flush/change/replace, no -batch, no netns exec.

ss._doc: No -K (kill sockets), -D (dump to a file), -F (read a filter file), -N (netns), -E (never returns), and no long options. Filter words cannot start with '-'.

systemctl._doc: No daemon-reload: it is a state change and stays a privileged-only command. No status (#817): it prints the unit's processes with their full command lines, and with no unit every process on the host. show takes a unit and a fixed property set (no Exec*/Environment*/Description: a transient unit's description is its command line). status stays on a privileged agent, for an admin.
systemctl.hint: systemctl status prints the unit's processes with their full command lines: use systemctl is-active UNIT, systemctl show UNIT -p ActiveState,SubState,MainPID,NRestarts,ActiveEnterTimestamp, or journalctl -u UNIT

journalctl._doc: Read flags only. No --flush/--rotate/--vacuum-*/--sync/--relinquish-var/--setup-keys/--update-catalog/-D/--file, no -f (never returns). Option values never start with '--', so a value slot cannot smuggle a flag. Output formats are the short family and cat only (#817): json, verbose and export print every entry's _CMDLINE (the logging process's full command line), and there is no -F/--field.
journalctl.hint: json, verbose and export output carry each process's full command line: use -o short (or short-iso, short-precise, with-unit, cat)

cat._doc: One absolute path, checked against read_paths exactly as read_file checks it.

docker._doc: Agent-side safe set only: kept out of the MCP read tier (docker inspect prints container environments).

_doc: #853: systemd unit files and drop-ins are readable (read_paths), and they carry other services'
secrets: Environment=TOKEN=..., SetCredential=, a WireGuard .netdev's PrivateKey=. The AGENT redacts
them before the content leaves the host, on every read_file and cat, privileged agent or not.
A file is unit-shaped when its path (as given or resolved) is under dirs, its name matches
unit_basename_regex, or its directory matches dropin_dir_regex. Its logical lines (a trailing
backslash continues a line) are rewritten: env_keys keep each variable NAME and lose its value
(Environment=TOKEN=<redacted>, quoted words keep their quote); credential_keys keep the credential
ID; secret_keys lose the whole value. Keys match case-insensitively. The control plane mirrors the
rewrite (adapters/readonly_policy.py) so drift and rollback can tell a redacted read from the bytes;
the shared corpus pins both to the same output.
exec_keys keep the program (and its systemd prefix characters -@:+!|) and lose every argument:
ExecStart=/usr/bin/app <arguments redacted> (args_mark). Arguments carry other services' secrets
(--token=...), the same class as #817. Rollback does not depend on this read: a privileged agent's
snapshot_file action returns the bytes write_config is about to replace (agent/go/snapshot.go).
file_keys and credential_file_keys name files a unit loads secrets FROM (EnvironmentFile=,
LoadCredential=ID:PATH, PrivateKeyFile=). The agent scans every unit-shaped file under dirs (plus
HP_AGENT_UNIT_DIRS) and refuses to read any file one of them names, wherever it sits, so an
environment file is unreadable even when nothing in its name says so. A % specifier in a named
path matches anything. Agent-only: the control plane cannot see the host's units.
